title: Independent and Dependent Quantities: Tables, Graphs and Equations
seo_title: Grade 6 Independent and Dependent Quantities Worksheets: Tables, Graphs and Equations (TEKS 6.6, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.4A compare two rules verbally, numerically, graphically, and symbolically in the form of y = ax or y = x + a in order to differentiate between additive and multiplicative relationships; 6.6A identify independent and dependent quantities from tables and graphs; 6.6B write an equation that represents the relationship between independent and dependent quantities from a table; 6.6C represent a given situation using verbal descriptions, tables, graphs, and equations in the form y = kx or y = x + b
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.4A and 6.6: independent and dependent quantities, equations y = kx and y = x + b from words, tables and graphs, and additive versus multiplicative relationships. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: y = kx is multiplicative; y = x + b is additive.
key_sub: The dependent quantity depends on the independent quantity. Check every pair.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The independent quantity changes on its own. The dependent quantity depends on it: the cost depends on the number of gallons.
  • A multiplicative relationship has the form y = kx: y is always k times x.
  • An additive relationship has the form y = x + b: y is always b more than x.
  • Check a rule with every pair in a table or graph.

Examples

Example

x: 1, 2, 3, 4 y: 7, 14, 21, 28

14 ÷ 2 = 7, 21 ÷ 3 = 7

Multiplicative

Answer: y = 7x

Example

x: 3, 4, 5 y: 10, 11, 12

10 − 3 = 7 for every pair

Additive

Answer: y = x + 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Switching the quantitiesAsk: which one depends on the other? That is the dependent quantity.
Checking only one pairy = 7x and y = x + 6 both give 1 → 7. Check the next pair too.
Using the change in y as the ruleIf y goes up by 7, test y = 7x and y = x + b.
